pass_a_gloss: [...] in these [words] at once the mystery, the deep and great, and needing the teaching from above. For it was revealed thus to the divine Peter. For the Word was and is God, equal in glory, and sharing the throne with the God and Father, and co-existing and co-eternal. And names before the becoming man, being in some way proper to his nature: God, and wisdom, and light, life, and power; and others besides these, which are found in the holy Letters. But since he let himself down into emptying, having come to be in likeness of man, and found in fashion as man, he receives the common name, that is, the Christ and Jesus, or the 'God with us'. The 'with us' signifying the [being] in our conditions. For it is written that, Behold the virgin will have in womb, and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel; and the blessed Gabriel, revealing to the holy virgin and Mother of God the mystery: Do not fear, he says, Mary. For you found grace with God, and behold you will conceive in womb, and you will bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus. For he himself will save his people from their sins. Have then the blessed angel and the prophet spoken voices not agreeing with one another? Not at all. For the divine prophet, speaking mysteries in spirit, announced beforehand God having come to be with us, naming him so both from the nature and from the economy with flesh. But the blessed angel put the name to him from the working; for he has saved his own people. Saviour then he has been called because of this. And indeed when he endured the birth according to flesh for us, the armies of the angels were announcing the birth as good news to the shepherds, saying: Do not fear; for behold we announce to you today a great joy, which is for all the people, that today was born a Saviour, who is Christ Lord, in a city of David. So Emmanuel, because being God by nature he came to be with us, that is, man; and Jesus, because it was needed that he save the [world] under heaven, being God and having become man. When then he came forth from the womb of his own mother, for he was born from her according to the flesh, then also his name was called. Unfitting then to God the Word, I say, before the birth according to flesh, is the name of Christ. For not yet anointed, how would he be called Christ? For when he came forth as man from the womb of a mother, then he receives the calling running together with the birth according to flesh. And he says his mouth was set like a sharp sword. True this too. For it is written somewhere about him, rather the prophet Isaiah himself says: And he will be girded with righteousness about the loin, and wrapped with truth about the [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … at once in these words the mystery, deep and great, which needs to be taught from above. For it was revealed in this way to the divine Peter (compare Matthew 16:16–17). For the Word was and is God, equal in glory with God the Father and sharing His throne, existing with Him and coeternal with Him. His names before the incarnation, those that are in some way proper to His nature, are God, Wisdom, Light, Life and Power, and besides these, others that are found in the sacred Scriptures.

But since He lowered Himself into self-emptying, being made in the likeness of man and found in form as a man (Philippians 2:7), He receives the common name, that is, Christ and Jesus, or else “God with us”; for “with us” means being in our condition. For it is written: “Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel” (Matthew 1:23; Isaiah 7:14). And the blessed Gabriel, revealing the mystery to the holy virgin, the Mother of God, says: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus” (Luke 1:30–31). “For he will save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).

Have the blessed angel and the prophet, then, spoken words that cannot be reconciled with each other? Not at all. For the divine prophet, speaking mysteries in the Spirit, announced beforehand God made to be with us, giving Him this name from His nature and from His dispensation in the flesh. The blessed angel, for his part, gave Him the name from what He does; for He has saved His own people. That is why He has been called Savior. Indeed, when He underwent birth according to the flesh for our sake, the hosts of angels brought the shepherds the good news of the birth, saying: “Do not be afraid; for behold, we bring you good news today of a great joy, which is for all the people: today a Savior has been born, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David” (Luke 2:10–11).

So He is Emmanuel because, being God by nature, He came to be with us, that is, became man; and Jesus because, being God and having become man, He was to save the world under heaven. When, then, He came forth from His own mother’s womb (for He was born of her according to the flesh), then His name was also called (Isaiah 49:1). So I say that the name Christ does not suit God the Word before His birth according to the flesh. For if He had not yet been anointed, how could He be called Christ? When He came forth as man from His mother’s womb, then He receives the name, together with His birth according to the flesh.

He says that His mouth was made like a sharp sword (Isaiah 49:2). This too is true. For it is written somewhere about Him, or rather the prophet Isaiah himself says: “And He shall be girded about the waist with righteousness, and wrapped in truth about the …” (Isaiah 11:5).

choices.why: ἰσοκλεής is equality of glory; it is not a second 'co-eternal', which follows separately.
The Word shares the Father's throne.

choices.english: the Word was and is God
choices.why: The phrase 'was and is God' is kept; it had been lost.
The angel names Christ from his saving work, not from the angel's own activity.
Cyril's title for the Virgin, kept as written.
